job.title: Residential Childcare Worker
job.description:
Support Worker - Children's Home
Location: Newbury
Hourly rate: National Living Wage, with rates of up to £13.15 per hour (depending on experience)
Job Type: Temporary, Agency Work
Shift Pattern: Flexible shifts available, including days, nights, sleep-ins, weekends and long days.
 
About the Role:
 
At First for Support, we're looking for compassionate and reliable Children's and Young People's Support Workers to join our growing team, providing temporary staffing to children's homes in and around Newbury.
 
As a Support Worker, you'll play an important role in supporting children and young people in residential care settings. You will help provide a safe, supportive and nurturing environment, build positive relationships and support young people with their daily routines, activities, education and emotional wellbeing. No two days are the same, giving you the opportunity to make a real difference while enjoying the flexibility that temporary work offers.
 
Your Responsibilities:
 
As a Children's Support Worker, your responsibilities may include:
· Provide high-quality care and support to children and young people.
· Build positive and trusting relationships.
· Support daily routines, activities and independence.
· Promote positive behaviour and emotional wellbeing.
· Follow care plans, risk assessments and safeguarding procedures.
· Complete accurate daily records and reports.
· Work effectively as part of a team and alongside other professionals.
 
What We're Looking For:
 
We're looking for candidates who:
· Have previous experience in a similar role as a Children's Support Worker.
· Are reliable, professional and able to work independently as well as part of a team.
· Have excellent communication and interpersonal skills and enjoy building meaningful relationships.
· Are Caring, patient and resilient.
· Are able to remain calm in challenging situations.
· Committed to safeguarding and promoting children's welfare.
 
In return, we offer weekly pay, flexible temporary shifts, ongoing support from a dedicated recruitment consultant and the opportunity to work with a variety of trusted care providers across Hampshire/Dorset/Berkshire, gaining valuable experience across different care settings.
 
If you're passionate about supporting children and young people and making a positive difference in their lives, we'd love to hear from you.
 
Apply today and a member of the First for Support team will be in touch to discuss your application.
 
Please note: First for Support is unable to offer sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK, as we do not provide Skilled Worker visa sponsorship.

job.title: Recovery Support Worker
job.description:
Job Title: Agency Support Worker - Recovery Support
Location: Bognor Regis
Pay Rate: £12.75-£13.00
Contract: Agency / Temporary
Hours: Flexible shifts, including days, nights, weekends and bank holidays.
 
We are seeking compassionate, reliable and experienced Agency Support Workers to provide recovery-focused support to residents living in hostel accommodation. The Support Worker will assist individuals experiencing homelessness, substance misuse, mental health difficulties and other complex needs, promoting recovery, independence and wellbeing.
 
The successful Support Worker will build positive relationships with residents, encourage engagement with recovery services, support independent living skills and help individuals work towards their personal goals. The role also involves maintaining a safe environment, completing support plans and daily records, following safeguarding procedures and managing challenging situations professionally.
 
Candidates should have previous experience as a Support Worker or in a similar role within hostels, homelessness services, substance misuse or mental health settings. A good understanding of safeguarding, professional boundaries, harm reduction and recovery-focused practice is desirable.
 
The ideal Support Worker will be empathetic, resilient, non-judgemental and committed to supporting vulnerable adults.
 
Flexibility to work agency shifts, including evenings and weekends, may be required.
 
If you are a dedicated Support Worker looking to make a positive difference in the lives of individuals on their recovery journey, we welcome your application.

job.title: Social Care Worker - Housing Support
job.description:
Contract type: Temporary/0 hour
Location: Greater Manchester
 
We are currently recruiting Temporary Support Workers to join our agency and provide support to the clients we work with. We are looking for caring, reliable, compassionate and dedicated support workers who are passionate about helping individuals maintain their independence, improve their well being and achieve positive outcomes in their lives.
 
As a Housing Support Worker, you will play an important role in supporting clients with a range of housing-related needs, helping them maintain suitable accommodation, develop independent living skills and work towards greater stability. Our support workers provide practical, emotional and person-centred support, ensuring that each client is treated with dignity, respect and understanding.
 
We are looking for flexible Temporary Support Workers who can respond to the needs of our agency and the clients we support. As a temporary support worker, you may be required to work with different clients in a variety of settings, providing consistent, professional and compassionate support tailored to individual needs.
 
The role may involve supporting clients to manage their accommodation, maintain a safe and suitable living environment, attend appointments, access relevant services and develop the confidence and skills needed to live independently. Support workers may also assist clients with budgeting, daily living activities, tenancy-related responsibilities and accessing community resources where appropriate.
 
Our support workers must be able to build positive professional relationships with clients, maintain clear and accurate records, follow individual support plans and work in line with safeguarding procedures, confidentiality requirements and organisational policies. We expect all support workers to demonstrate professionalism, patience, empathy and a genuine commitment to improving the lives of the people they support.
 
Previous experience in housing support, supported accommodation, health and social care or a similar support worker role would be advantageous. However, we welcome applications from individuals who have the right attitude, a willingness to learn and a strong commitment to providing high-quality support. Good communication skills, reliability, flexibility and the ability to work independently and as part of a team are essential.
 
As an agency, we understand the importance of having dependable support workers who can adapt to changing client needs and provide a consistent standard of care and support. We are therefore seeking temporary support workers who are available to work flexibly and are committed to delivering a positive experience for every client they support.
 
If you are a compassionate Housing Support Worker or Temporary Support Worker looking for an opportunity to make a meaningful difference, we would love to hear from you. Join our agency and become part of a team dedicated to empowering clients, promoting independence and supporting people to achieve better housing and life outcomes.
 
Apply today to join our team of dedicated support workers and help us make a real difference in the lives of the clients we support.

job.title: Registered Manager - Children's Home
job.description:
Registered Manager Children's Residential Home
Salary: up to £55,000 per annum
Location: Sway, Lymington, SO41


We are seeking a dedicated and experienced Registered Manager or a Deputy Manager who is looking to step up to support the effective leadership of a child-centred residential home that is currently home to 2 children. This role is key to ensuring the home consistently meets Ofsted regulations, delivers high-quality care, and promotes positive outcomes for children.


Working as the Registered Manager, you will help maintain a safe, nurturing, and stable environment, underpinned by therapeutic practice and strong safeguarding principles.


Key Responsibilities


·Safeguard and promote the welfare of children in line with legislation and best practice
·Lead, supervise, and develop the staff team to deliver consistently high standards of care
·Contribute to care planning, risk management, and regulatory compliance
·Participate in the on-call rota when required
 
Requirements


·Minimum 2 year's experience in a children's residential management role
·Strong knowledge of Ofsted standards, safeguarding, and quality assurance
·Hold a either a Level 3 NVQ or Level 5 Diploma in Leadership & Management
·Profficient in de-escalation of challenging behaviours
·Full UK driving licence


Working hours are Monday to Friday 0900-1700 however this may vary in accordance with the needs of the home with sleep ins paid in addition at £55 per sleep.


If you are passionate about delivering high-quality, child-focused care as a Registered Manager and ready to take the next step in your leadership career, please APPLY NOW!

job.title: Support Worker
job.description:
Support Worker (Adults)
 
Location: Hampshire/Dorset (Southampton, Portsmouth and Bournemouth)
Salary: National Living Wage, with rates of up to £14.50 per hour (depending on experience)
Job Type: Temporary
Shift Pattern: Flexible shifts available, including days, nights, sleep-ins, weekends and long days.
 
About the Role
 
At First for Support, we're looking for compassionate and reliable Support Workers to join our growing team, providing temporary staffing support to a range of adult care services across Hampshire.
As a Support Worker, you'll play an important role in helping adults live as independently as possible while promoting dignity, respect and choice. Working across residential services, supported living and other care settings, no two days are the same, giving you the opportunity to make a real difference while enjoying the flexibility that temporary work offers.
Your Responsibilities
 
As a Support Worker, your responsibilities may include:
 
·Providing high-quality, person-centred support.
·Assisting with personal care where required.
·Supporting individuals with daily living activities, including cooking, cleaning and shopping.
·Encouraging independence and promoting choice.
·Supporting individuals to access the local community, appointments and social activities.
·Administering or assisting with medication in line with training and company procedures.
·Maintaining accurate care records and reporting any concerns.
·Promoting safeguarding, dignity, equality and inclusion at all times.
You may support adults with a range of needs, including dementia, learning disabilities, autism, mental health needs, physical disabilities and other complex needs.
 
What We're Looking For
 
We're looking for candidates who:
·Have previous experience in a Care or Support Worker role.
·Have experience supporting adults and/or older people with a range of complex needs, including dementia, learning disabilities, autism and mental health needs.
·Are caring, patient, compassionate and enthusiastic about making a positive difference.
·Are reliable, professional and able to work independently as well as part of a team.
·Have excellent communication and interpersonal skills and enjoy building meaningful relationships.
·Understand person-centred care and promoting dignity, choice and independence.
In return, we offer weekly pay, flexible temporary shifts, ongoing support from a dedicated recruitment consultant and the opportunity to work with a variety of trusted care providers across Hampshire, gaining valuable experience across different care settings.
 
Apply Today
 
If you're passionate about supporting adults and making a positive difference in their lives, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and a member of the First for Support team will be in touch to discuss your application.
 
Please note: First for Support is unable to offer sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK, as we do not provide Skilled Worker visa sponsorship.

job.title: Deputy Manager
job.description:
Deputy Manager - Supported Accommodation
Canterbury | £38,000-£40,000 | 6-Month FTC
First for Support are currently seeking an experienced Deputy Manager to join a supportive team in Canterbury.
This is an exciting opportunity to take a key leadership role across two supported accommodation homes, supporting young people aged 16-21, including looked-after children and care leavers.
You'll manage and support a team of 6 Support Workers, helping to ensure the young people receive high-quality, consistent and person-centred support.


What We're Looking For
We're looking for an experienced Deputy Manager or Senior Support Worker with strong leadership experience.
You'll need:
·Experience supporting young people aged 16-21
·Strong team leadership and management skills
·Experience working with looked-after children and/or care leavers
·Excellent communication and organisational skills
·A person-centred approach and genuine commitment to young people's wellbeing


What's on Offer?
·£38,000-£40,000 salary
·6-month FTC or temporary placement
·Monday-Friday working hours
·Additional leave on your birthday
·Discounts scheme
·Opportunity to make a real difference to young people's lives
